items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: I became friends with him, and he showed me the first bass line that I ever played, on a blues in F.

ctx.x: I’m going to take a guess that when you were describing playing with Don Alias every day, that’s where some of your left hand bass playing came from?

Well it certainly probably strengthened at that point. My feeling for the phrasing and time in general, you know, it was like an awakening aspect of playing time playing with Don, that I really hadn’t experienced at that level. But the bass line really came before then. There was an organ player that used to come through the area by the name of Wendell Byrd and he was quite notorious. And at the time there was a couple of clubs around Central New York, Birdland in Utica was one and Benevin’s Lounge in Rome. And…

put the matchbook cover between keys to hold the key down while you’re playing underneath it and then you’d get up and leave and the organ would still be playing. You know the drummer would solo for 45 minutes. Sometimes you’d go to a bar and have a couple of drinks. A few times he actually just went home. And then finally the drummer would get tired and turn off the organ.
